title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. The section studies an 'equation des lacets' (loop equation) attached to the profinite group \hat G^+_{0,3}. Its presentation <rho, sigma | rho^3 = sigma^2 = 1> identifies it with the profinite completion of Z/3 * Z/2 = PSL_2(Z). This is the orbifold fundamental group of (P^1 - {0,1,infinity})/S_3, equivalently of the coarse M_{1,1}, and it is an extension of S_3 by \hat F_2 = \hat G_{0,3}.

The automorphisms considered are of the form u(rho) = xi rho, u(sigma) = eta sigma. On the previous page these are written u(rho) = int(f^{-1})(xi rho) and so on. Sigma_{rho,sigma} is the set of admissible pairs (xi, eta), and Sigma^eff is the subset actually realised by an automorphism.

Top of page. This completes the previous remark, which drops hypothesis (20)b) and replaces it by the 'effective' variants. The isomorphism (62) replaces the earlier (38). It identifies a group S_0 Gamma^0_{rho,sigma} of triples (u, a, b) (classes of an automorphism and two conjugating elements) with a group S_0 G^#_{rho,sigma} of pairs, via (u, a, b) -> (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}).

(63) gives the basic exact sequence 1 -> \hat G^+_{0,3} -> M^~_{rho,sigma} -> Gamma^~_{0,3}/Gamma^~_Q -> 1. Here M^~ is a group of (classes of) automorphisms of \hat G^+_{0,3} preserving the conjugacy classes of rho and sigma up to the allowed twisting. Its quotient is the 'Teichmuller-type' group Gamma^~_{0,3} modulo the Galois part, i.e. a GT-like group.

(64) defines Gamma^{•~} as the kernel of a character Gamma^~_{0,3} -> {±1} (a crossed-out (Z/3)^* is visible), namely {gamma | mu(gamma) ≡ 1 mod 3}. Here mu is the cyclotomic-type character (lambda in GT language). Since rho has order 3, an automorphism sends rho to a conjugate of rho^{mu}, and mu mod 3 is ±1. The condition mu ≡ 1 mod 3 therefore singles out the index-≤2 subgroup that sends rho to a conjugate of rho itself rather than of rho^{-1}. That is exactly what the form u(rho) = xi rho presupposes.

(65) defines M^{•~}_{0,3} as the inverse image of this subgroup in M^~_{0,3}.

(66)-(68) start a new topic: finite (or profinite) quotients psi : \hat G^+_{0,3} ->> G. Such a quotient amounts to a pair rho_G, sigma_G with rho_G^3 = sigma_G^2 = 1, i.e. a (2,3)-generated profinite group. Equivalently it is a normal open subgroup of \hat PSL_2(Z), i.e. a regular dessin / modular-curve-type cover.

The next page defines psi to be 'effective' when, for every u in M', the induced pair (xi_G, eta_G) is realised by an automorphism u_G of G with u_G psi = psi u. This is equivalent to M' stabilising Ker psi. Several equivalent conditions are listed (a), (b), (b'), (c), (c')). The purpose is to transport the loop-equation formalism to finite quotients, i.e. to study the action of the GT-like group on finite (2,3)-generated quotients and on their automorphisms.
errors: (64): the transcription has Gamma^{•~}_Q on the left, while (65) uses Gamma^{•~}_{0,3}. The defined group is a subgroup of Gamma^~_{0,3}, so the notation is inconsistent; Gamma^•_{0,3} is evidently meant.

(66)-(68): a continuous homomorphism from \hat G^+_{0,3} corresponds to two elements with rho_G^3 = sigma_G^2 = 1. Surjectivity additionally requires that rho_G, sigma_G topologically generate G. This condition is omitted, presumably implicitly assumed.
(64): the target written {±1} is really (Z/3)^* ≅ {±1}, and the condition 'mu ≡ 1 (3)' is consistent with that. The crossed-out material suggests hesitation about the target.

ideas.what: Presenting the profinite completion of Z/3*Z/2 (orbifold pi_1 of (P^1-{0,1,inf})/S_3) as the basic object, with automorphisms normalised by u(rho)=xi rho, u(sigma)=eta sigma, and an exact sequence with a GT-type quotient
ideas.modern_name: GT action on \hat PSL_2(Z) / \hat B_3 (level (1,1) of the Teichmuller tower)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the (0,3)/(1,1) modular levels; this specific formalism is unpublished as far as I know

ideas.what: Index-2 subgroup of the GT-like group defined by the cyclotomic-type character mu ≡ 1 mod 3, ensuring rho maps to a conjugate of rho rather than rho^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: restriction to lambda ≡ 1 mod 3 (kernel of the character to (Z/3)^*)
ideas.usually_credited_to: implicit in GT literature (lambda mod 3/mod 6 considerations)

ideas.what: Surjections of \hat PSL_2(Z) onto profinite G, i.e. pairs (rho_G, sigma_G) of orders dividing 3 and 2 (next page: 'effective' quotients whose kernel is stable under the GT-like group)
ideas.modern_name: (2,3)-generated groups / regular dessins; GT- or Galois-stable normal subgroups; GT-shadows
ideas.usually_credited_to: dessins: Grothendieck, Jones-Singerman, Schneps; GT-shadows: Dolgushev and coauthors (2020s)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme discusses dessins and Galois action, not this effectivity notion

missed.claim: The notion of an 'effective' finite quotient psi : \hat G^+_{0,3} -> G, together with the induced pairs (xi_G, eta_G) solving the loop equation in G, anticipates the finite-level approximation of GT. This is close in spirit to Dolgushev's 'GT-shadows' (solutions of the GT relations modulo a finite-index normal subgroup) and to the question of which finite-level solutions lift ('charming' GT-shadows). Here it is done for \hat PSL_2(Z) = <rho,sigma | rho^3 = sigma^2 = 1> rather than for PB_4 / F_2.
missed.quote: Soit G un groupe profini, et (66) psi : \hat G^+_{0,3} -> G ... ce qui revient à se donner deux éléments rho_G, sigma_G ... rho_G^3 = sigma_G^2 = 1
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It suggests a PSL_2(Z)-level version of GT-shadow theory for (2,3)-generated finite groups, with an explicit criterion for effectivity: stability of Ker psi under M'. This could complement current computational work on GT-shadows.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a mostly set-up page: notation, a restricted subgroup via mu ≡ 1 mod 3, and the start of a study of finite (2,3)-generated quotients. The finite-level 'effective quotient' viewpoint foreshadows GT-shadows, but the page itself only introduces definitions.
transcription_corrections: Line 1 likely reads 'de groupes ... : S_0 G_{rho,sigma}, par l'isomorphisme (qui remplace (38))'. The top-right of (62) reads '#' (S_0 G^#_{rho,sigma}).

(64): the left side is Gamma^{•~}, with a circled subscript probably meant as 0,3 (see (65)). The target of the map is {±1} = (Z/3)^*, with a crossed-out alternative. The condition is mu(gamma) ≡ 1 (3).
(65): before 'et soit' there is a crossed-out M''^~_{0,3}; the text continues 'Image inverse de Gamma^{•~}_{0,3} dans M^~_{0,3}'.
(66): 'un homom. continu surjectif', with 'continu' added above the line.
(67): parenthetical 'leurs images de rho, sigma par psi', followed by 'satisfaisant'.
